title: DUET study - Dyadic coping and parental adjustment during the transition to parenthood
summary: With this study, we want to investigate the influence of stress coping in couples during the transition to parenthood. Pregnancy, childbirth, and the early postpartum period can pose a number of challenges for (expectant) parents. This can lead to stress, which, if not managed well, can even lead to mental health problems such as depression or anxiety disorders. Coping with stress together as a couple can be an important resource in this context. With this study, we aim to systematically record and investigate these factors using questionnaires. At four measurement points (upon registration of birth between the 28th and 37th week of pregnancy, 8-48 hours after birth, 6 weeks and 6 months after birth), couples receive questionnaires on relevant areas such as joint stress coping, subjective stress perception, depressive symptoms, anxiety, mental well-being, relationship satisfaction and satisfaction with sexuality, attachment style, pre- and postnatal attachment to the child, sleep quality and quantity, personality traits, resilience, personality anxiety, and self-efficacy. In addition, sociodemographic data and information on pregnancy and birth are collected.
conditions: Mental health of (expectand) parents during the transition to parenthood

interventions.name: Pregnant individuals in their first or second pregnancy and their partners will be surveyed using questionnaires at four measurement time points (at birth registration between 28th and 37th week of gestation, 8-48 h postpartum, 6 weeks postpartum, 6 months postpartum).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Pregnant women in their first or second pregnancy who are in the last trimester and wish to give birth vaginally; pregnant women must be in a relationship; sufficient German language skills of the pregnant woman and her partner to participate in the questionnaire survey; written informed consent to participate in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
Serious comorbidities in pregnant women (as assessed by the physician); known serious illnesses of the child that require transfer of the newborn to the pediatric ward; lack of mental, physical, or linguistic ability of the pregnant woman and/or her partner to participate in the questionnaire survey.
